faqs.question: When is Ganesh Chaturthi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on Monday 14 September. The festival runs through to visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi, Friday 25 September 2026, so greeting images circulate across those eleven days rather than on a single morning.

faqs.question: What size should a Happy Ganesh Chaturthi image be for a WhatsApp status?
faqs.answer: Export at 1080 x 1920 pixels, the full-screen portrait shape a status occupies. Matching the destination shape means the platform only recompresses your file instead of also cropping it, which is where most of the visible damage happens.

faqs.question: Why do my Ganpati photos look blurry after I send them on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Because the file you sent is not the file that arrives. A 2021 media-forensics survey records that sharing platforms including WhatsApp resize and re-encode images on upload under their own rules, and that is what softens the detail in a mandap photograph.

faqs.question: How do I send a Ganesh Chaturthi image without losing quality?
faqs.answer: Attach it as a document rather than as a photo, which preserves the original bytes. It is worth doing for a picture someone might print, and pointless for a greeting graphic that will be glanced at once.

faqs.question: Can I put someone's name on a Happy Ganesh Chaturthi image?
faqs.answer: Yes, most name tools bake the name into the JPEG before you download it. The catch is that it is baked in: a typo means generating the file again, and a second recipient means a second file.

faqs.question: Are the ganpati bappa photos I forward actually mine?
faqs.answer: Almost never. In a study of 1,101 public WhatsApp groups, 54.5% of image messages carried the Forwarded label, and platforms strip out metadata such as capture time and location on upload, so nothing about origin travels with the file.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Ganesh Chaturthi image and a shareable page?
faqs.answer: An image is a finished file the recipient looks at. A page is a link they open and act on, and you can still edit it after sending, which no JPEG allows.

faqs.question: Is it rude to forward the same Ganesh Chaturthi image to everyone?
faqs.answer: Not in a large group, where nobody expects the message to be about them. It reads badly one to one, because forwarding is the default behaviour for images on WhatsApp and most people can tell a forward from something made for them.

faqs.question: What size should a Happy Ganesh Chaturthi banner be for printing?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the board you are ordering. A 6ft x 3ft flex is 18 square feet, and most Indian print shops quote per square foot. Always design from the original artwork, never from a copy that has been through a chat app.

faqs.question: Can I keep a Ganesh Chaturthi page private?
faqs.answer: Yes, by setting a password on it. Platform-wide across all 3,860 SubhSandesh pages and 15 page types, 42.1% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it.

faqs.question: How late can I send Ganesh Chaturthi wishes?
faqs.answer: Any time between 14 and 25 September 2026 reads as timely, because the festival runs to visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi. A message on visarjan day is not late; it is just a different moment.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Images: What Actually Lands on WhatsApp

Ganesh Chaturthi images are the fastest greeting you can send and the least durable one you can send. Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on Monday 14 September, with visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi, Friday 25 September, so most of these files will be forwarded across those eleven days and never opened again. An image cannot be edited after it leaves your phone, cannot be opened as anything except a picture, and is resized and re-encoded before it reaches the other person. Where you want the recipient to do something rather than look at something, a shareable page holds up better: across all 3,860 pages SubhSandesh has created since March 2026, spanning 15 page types, 49.6% of the 45,656 recorded views were on a phone, and 96.1% of started pages were finished and shared. Below: five image formats, what each one gives up, and the four cases where an image is still the right call.

## What counts as a Ganesh Chaturthi image?

A Ganesh Chaturthi image is a static JPEG or PNG carrying Ganpati artwork or a photograph plus a short greeting line, sized for a chat window, a 1080 × 1920 status screen or a print sheet. It is a finished file, not a document — whatever it says is what it will say forever.

Four sub-types account for almost everything people search for. Stock or free-download artwork of the deity. A happy Ganesh Chaturthi image with a name typed onto it. A ganpati bappa photo shot at your own mandap or someone else's. And a happy Ganesh Chaturthi banner or poster, which is the same file at print dimensions with a logo on it. They differ in who made them, not in what they can do once sent.

## 5 Ganesh Chaturthi image formats, and what each one gives up

Each entry below covers the same four things: what it is, who it suits, what it costs, and what it loses.

### 1. Free stock Ganpati artwork

Illustrated or rendered Ganesha files from a stock library, downloaded and forwarded unchanged. Suits a large WhatsApp group or a broadcast list where nobody expects the message to be about them specifically. Costs nothing beyond a minute of searching. What it loses is authorship — the same file is going out from thousands of other phones on 14 September, and the recipient has no way to tell whether you chose it or forwarded it.

### 2. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi images with a name on them

A template where you type a name into a box and download a personalised JPEG. Suits one named recipient — a parent, a boss, a client. Costs nothing on most tools. What it loses is everything after the download: the name is baked into the pixels, so a typo means starting again, and a second recipient means a second file. Personalisation that happens before sending is not personalisation the recipient can see you doing.

### 3. Ganpati bappa photos from your own mandap

A photograph you took of your own idol, decoration or aarti thali. Suits family and close friends, and it is the only image format nobody else on your contact list can send. Costs nothing but timing — the usable frames come at the evening aarti, not at noon. What it loses is resolution, because your camera's original file is not what arrives; see the next section.

### 4. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi banner or poster

The same artwork laid out at print or hoarding dimensions, usually with a mandal name, a sponsor logo or a business address. Suits mandals, shops and companies. Costs nothing to design and then whatever your local flex shop charges per square foot — a 6ft × 3ft board is 18 square feet. What it loses is any digital function at all — a poster is a poster, and the WhatsApp version of it will be unreadably compressed at that aspect ratio.

### 5. A shareable Ganesh Chaturthi page instead of an image

A link the recipient opens, where the greeting is something they perform rather than view. Suits one person or a small group you actually want a response from. Costs nothing but the time to add your photo and write the card. What it loses is offline reach — no signal, no page — and it will not paste into an Instagram story as a picture, so you still need an image for that.

## Why the image you forward is almost never the image you made

Forwarding, not composing, is the default behaviour for images on WhatsApp. In a study of 9.78 million messages from 1,101 public WhatsApp groups, [54.5% of image messages carried WhatsApp's "Forwarded" label](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/31372), against 65% for videos and a negligible share for plain text — the authors' reading is that producing an image takes effort, so people pass one along instead. Single images in that dataset appeared over a thousand times.

That research covers Brazilian political groups, so treat the exact figure as indicative rather than Indian. The Indian picture is similar in shape. Chauchard and Garimella hand-coded [around 36,000 images from 533 partisan WhatsApp threads across Uttar Pradesh](https://journalqd.org/article/view/2690) over nine months and found that the largest share was not political at all but phatic or entertainment content, much of it religion-related — greeting images doing social maintenance work rather than argument.

Recycled images also lose their history. In a separate analysis of 1.6 million images from more than 5,000 Indian public groups, [old images taken out of context made up roughly 34% of the misinformation set](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/images-and-misinformation-in-political-groups-evidence-from-whatsapp-in-india/). A festival greeting is harmless by comparison, but the mechanism is the same: once a JPEG is loose, nothing travels with it.

## What WhatsApp does to a Ganesh Chaturthi image before it arrives

Your file is not delivered as you made it. A 2021 survey of media forensics on social platforms records that sharing services including WhatsApp [apply resizing and JPEG recompression on upload](https://jis-eurasipjournals.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s13635-021-00117-2), with platform-specific rules, and that they usually strip optional metadata fields such as acquisition time, GPS coordinates and the acquiring device. That is why a sharp mandap photo arrives soft, and why nobody can prove the photo was yours.

Three practical consequences. Shoot and export at the destination's shape — 1080 × 1920 for a status, 1080 × 1080 for a feed post — so the platform is not both resizing and cropping. Send an important photo as a document rather than as a photo when you want the original bytes to survive. And do not use a compressed WhatsApp image as the source file for a printed banner; go back to the original before it went through any chat app.

## Image, or a page: what each format can actually do

The five columns people actually care about are cost, effort, whether the recipient can act on it, whether it stays private, and whether it survives the festival. The last column below is SubhSandesh's own platform-wide data, measured on 8 September 2026 across all 15 page types — there is no Ganesh-specific figure yet, because the Ganesh template shipped days ago.

| What you want the greeting to do | A JPEG | A shareable page | SubhSandesh platform-wide figure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open on a phone with nothing installed | Yes | Yes | 49.6% of 45,656 views are on a phone |
| Stay private to one person | No | Yes | 42.1% of creators password-protect before sharing (1,625 of 3,860) |
| Get finished rather than abandoned | Yes | Mostly | 96.1% of started pages are published and shared (3,708 of 3,860) |
| Be changed after you've already sent it | No | Yes | median 6.8 hours between a page's first save and last edit (n=1,065) |
| Carry your own photo and your own mandap | Only if you shot it | Yes | 3,860 pages created since 12 March 2026 across 15 page types |

The takeaway is narrow: an image wins on reach and loses on everything that happens after delivery. If you want the second column, the [Ganesh Chaturthi page where the recipient offers the durva and modak themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) is the version of this greeting they perform rather than scroll past — they circle the aarti thali, Karpur Gauram plays, and they write their own prarthana back to you.

## When a Ganesh Chaturthi image is the right choice, and when we are not

Four cases where the image wins outright. A broadcast to 200 contacts, where a link would read as marketing. An Instagram story, where a URL is dead weight and a picture is the format. A printed banner or poster at the mandap. And a recipient on a feature phone, on patchy data, or one who simply will not tap an unfamiliar link — 49.6% of our views are on a phone platform-wide, which also means half are not, and a page assumes a browser.

And the honest limit on our side. A page cannot replace standing in the mandap queue at 9 pm, it cannot put a modak in anyone's hand, and it cannot do the visarjan procession on 25 September. If you are in the same city as the person, go. If you are not, the [full list of SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers occasions beyond this one, but none of them are a substitute for showing up.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

failed.why: The five H3 blocks each run to four sentences because page-structure.md requires every H3 to cover the same four fields in the same order (what it is / who it suits / cost / what it loses). The two rules conflict; the H3 consistency rule was kept because it is what makes the list machine-extractable. Every other paragraph in the post is two or three sentences.

failed.why: Four outbound links, but two were not verified against the exact URL linked. journalqd.org's PDF endpoint timed out on three attempts, so the Chauchard & Garimella claim is taken from the abstract on the article landing page only. The Pasquini survey was read in full, but from the author copy at iris.uniroma1.it (handle 11573/1622925); the SpringerOpen URL that the body links serves a bot challenge to scripted fetches. Closing this needs a re-fetch of both from a normal browser session.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine asked what a Ganesh Chaturthi image can and cannot do has nothing else to cite: the ten pages competing for this keyword are stock grids, free-download libraries and name-typing tools with no third-party data on any of them, and this is the only one that pairs peer-reviewed figures on WhatsApp image forwarding and platform recompression with first-party page data no competitor can publish. Two real weaknesses: every SubhSandesh number here is platform-wide across 15 page types rather than Ganesh-specific, because the template shipped days ago with zero pages, and three of the four studies were run on political rather than festival groups, which the body says out loud. Domain authority is far below Getty, Adobe and the entrenched wishes farms, so this is a months-long play at best and the head term 'ganesh chaturthi images' is realistically unwinnable — the long-tail variants folded in here are the winnable part.
